type_schema.description:
NEAR Account Identifier.

This is a unique, syntactically valid, human-readable account identifier on the NEAR network.

[See the crate-level docs for information about validation.](index.html#account-id-rules)

Also see [Error kind precedence](AccountId#error-kind-precedence).

## Examples

``` use near_account_id::AccountId;

let alice: AccountId = "alice.near".parse().unwrap();

assert!("ƒelicia.near".parse::<AccountId>().is_err()); // (ƒ is not f) ```

functions.name: claim_link
functions.doc:
Pays a Funded link to `receiver_id`. Authorized by the ed25519 signature of the link key over
 `pot-claim:v1:<hub>:<pot>:<request_id>:<receiver_id>`, never by the caller (works through a
 NEP-366 delegate from a brand-new 0-NEAR account, or relayer-signed). The hub registers the
 receiver on the token (≤ 0.00125 NEAR, refunded by the token if already registered); a direct
 unsponsored caller attaches it.

functions.name: migrate
functions.doc:
Wave 4 state migration (hub 1.0.0 → 1.1.0): appends the three side maps. Old records are
 untouched (their Borsh layouts are frozen); Pots without a `PotExt` keep the 1.0.0 rules.
 Deploy + migrate in ONE transaction (DeployContract + FunctionCall), see notes/contracts-wave4.md.

functions.name: propose_sweep
functions.doc:
M-2: pays out USDC left in a Closed Pot's DAO (sent straight to it after the close, or a link
 payment the token returned late). In a v3 / v4 Pot nobody but the hub can propose anything, so
 without this such money would be stuck. Anyone may ask; the hub reads the DAO's whole USDC
 balance and proposes paying it out like the close (pro-rata to contributions; equally when
 nobody contributed). Members approve it by majority, like a close. One per Pot per day; the
 caller pays the proposal's storage unless a relayer signs.

 pro-rata refund close as the hub (the `propose_close` chain); phase 2 (that close pending, or
 Failed) approves / finalizes it as rulebot, then maps the result like `sync`. Call it twice.

This is a unique, syntactically valid, human-readable account identifier on the NEAR network.

[See the crate-level docs for information about validation.](index.html#account-id-rules)

Also see [Error kind precedence](AccountId#error-kind-precedence).

## Examples

``` use near_account_id::AccountId;

let alice: AccountId = "alice.near".parse().unwrap();

assert!("ƒelicia.near".parse::<AccountId>().is_err()); // (ƒ is not f) ```
